newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Business of closed Mauritian bank taken over.
newsitem.headline: Business of closed Mauritian bank taken over.

text.p: Delphis Bank said on Monday it had taken over the banking business of another Mauritian commercial bank, Union International Bank, which was ordered closed last May by the Central Bank of Mauritius.

"The Delphis Bank Limited is pleased to announce that its offer for the acquisition of the banking business of Union Bank International Limited (in liquidation) has been accepted by the Liquidator and sanctioned by the Master and Registrar in Bankruptcy Court," Delphis said in a statement.
Union Bank International was ordered to cease business on May 4 for alleged irregularities and its banking license was revoked on August 3.
Delphis Bank said it would employ all 75 Union Bank staff below senior management and honour all the deposit liabilities of the defunct bank.
With the takeover, Delphis Bank's existing network of three branches across the island will expand to eight.
Delphis Bank is controlled by Kenyan businessman Ketan Somaia.
